objectives.text: APPLY Newton's laws of motion to a body.

enabling.text: STATE Newton's first law of motion.
STATE Newton's second law of motion.
STATE Newton's third law of motion.
STATE Newton's law of universal gravitation.
Using the conservation of momentum, CALCULATE the velocity for an object (or objects) following a collision of two objects.

passages.quote: an object remains at rest (if originally at rest) or moves in a straight line with constant velocity if the net force on it is zero.
the acceleration of a body is proportional to the net (i.e., sum or resultant) force acting on it and in the direction of that net force.
if a body exerts a force on a second body, the second body exerts an equal and opposite force on the first.
forces always occur in pairs of equal and opposite forces.
For any two masses, the force is directly proportional to the product of the two masses and is inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them.
It is the result of the product of the body's mass and the velocity at which it is moving.
Momentum is a vector quantity since it results from the velocity of the object.
The rate at which momentum changes with time is equal to the net force applied to an object.
if no net external force acts upon an object, the momentum of the object remains constant.
In an elastic collision, both momentum and kinetic energy (i.e., energy due to an objects velocity) are conserved.
In an inelastic collision, momentum is conserved, but system kinetic energy is not conserved.
the sum of a system's initial momentum is equal to the sum of a system's final momentum.

body.text: Newton's first law of motion states:
Newton's second law states:
F = ma
F is force, m is mass, and a is acceleration. This law is used to define force units.
For an object's weight at the surface of the earth, the acceleration is g, which equals 9.8 m/sec² or 32.17 ft/sec², so the equation becomes F = mg.
Newton's third law of motion states:
It has also been stated as, for every action there is an equal and opposite reaction.

checks.q: Under Newton's second law, the acceleration of a body is:
o: Proportional to the net force and in the direction of that net force
Inversely proportional to the net force
Proportional to the net force and opposite to its direction
checks.x: The acceleration of a body is proportional to the net force acting on it and in the direction of that net force.

body.text: Each mass in the universe exerts a mutual, attractive gravitational force on every other mass.
F = G m1 m2 / r²
G is the universal constant of gravitation, m1 and m2 are the two masses, and r is the distance between their centers.
The value of g varies with altitude, but 30 km of height only changes it from 9.8 m/sec² to 9.7 m/sec². So g is normally treated as a constant for objects close to the surface of the earth.

checks.q: The distance between two masses is doubled. What happens to the gravitational force between them?
o: It is cut to one fourth
checks.x: The force is inversely proportional to the square of the distance. Doubling the distance divides the force by 2², which is 4.

body.text: Momentum is, in a sense, the measure of the motion of a moving body.
P = mv
If different momentum quantities are added vectorially, the direction of each must be taken into account.
F = ΔP / Δt

checks.q: What is the momentum of a 10 lbm object moving at 5 ft/sec?

body.text: If force is equal to zero, then ΔP = 0. This is most important for collisions and explosions, where the external force is negligible.
When a gun is fired, the momentum of the recoiling gun is equal and opposite to the momentum of the bullet.
When two bodies collide and have identical final velocities:
m1v1 + m2v2 = (m1 + m2)vf

body.alt: Two railroad cars before a collision with velocities v1 and v2, and after it coupled and moving together at vf.

checks.q: Which statement is true of an inelastic collision?
o: Momentum and kinetic energy are both conserved
Neither momentum nor kinetic energy is conserved
Kinetic energy is conserved, but momentum is not
Momentum is conserved, but system kinetic energy is not
checks.x: In an inelastic collision, momentum is conserved, but system kinetic energy is not conserved.

examples.problem: Car 1 (2300 lbm) moves at 29 ft/sec and overtakes car 2 (2800 lbm) moving at 11 ft/sec. They couple. Calculate the final velocity.

facts.q: How is force related to the rate of change of momentum?
facts.a: The rate at which momentum changes with time is equal to the net force applied to an object.

facts.q: Why is momentum a vector quantity?
facts.a: It results from the velocity of the object.

facts.q: What is conserved in an elastic collision?

facts.a: The acceleration of a body is proportional to the net force acting on it and in the direction of that net force.

facts.q: State the universal law of gravitation for two masses.
facts.a: The force is directly proportional to the product of the two masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them.

summary.text: An object remains at rest or moves in a straight line with constant velocity if the net force on it is zero.
The forces of action and reaction between interacting bodies are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction.
Gravitational force is directly proportional to the product of the two masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them.
Momentum is the product of a body's mass and its velocity, P = mv.
If no net external force acts upon a system, the momentum of the system remains constant.
